name: Kimura System
keyCorrections: If they straighten their arm, you lost the angle — pull their elbow toward you to re-bend the arm.
If you can't finish, your rotation is insufficient — bring their elbow toward your hips while rotating.
If they grab their own leg to defend, switch to the armbar or back take.
description: Use the kimura grip as a control hub for sweeps, passes, back takes, or finishes — the kimura is a position, not just a submission.
shortInstruction: Grip the wrist, figure-four the arm, rotate the shoulder — the kimura is control first, submission second.
summary: The kimura is the most versatile submission in no-gi BJJ. The Kimura grip (one hand holding their same-side wrist, the other arm threading through to grab your own wrist) is more commonly used as a control position than as a submission. From the Kimura grip, you can: sweep, pass the guard, take the back, or finish the shoulder lock. The system is based on isolating one of their arms and using it as a handle to control their entire body.
whyItWorks: The Kimura grip creates a figure-four lock on their arm that they cannot easily break — once locked, you control their shoulder.
Using their arm as a 'handle' gives you control over their entire body — when you move their arm, their body follows.
The Kimura system works from almost every position: guard, side control, half guard, mount, and transitions.
Danaher principle: the Kimura is the most versatile submission in BJJ because it is also the best control position.
commonMistakes: Chasing the submission before establishing control — the Kimura is a control position first.
Letting the opponent straighten their arm — a straight arm escapes the Kimura lock.
Using only arm strength instead of body rotation — the Kimura finish comes from rotating your hips.
Losing the wrist grip — the wrist grip is the anchor of the entire system.
coachingCues: Kimura is control — the submission is just one option.
Control the wrist, lock the figure-four, own their body.
If you have the Kimura grip, you have the position — now choose your attack.
Rotate the shoulder, not the arm — shoulder rotation is the finish.
safetySummary: The Kimura applies rotational pressure to the shoulder and elbow — apply gradually.
Do not crank the shoulder lock — shoulder injuries can take months to recover.
Release immediately on tap — the Kimura can cause serious shoulder damage with minimal force.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Secure Kimura grip (wrist control + figure-four): use their arm as a handle → choose your attack based on their reaction.

decisionTree.action: They resist → Kimura submission. Option 2: They post → sweep to top.
They turn away → take the back. Option 4: They play dead → pass the guard.

moneyDetails: Your wrist grip must be strong — four fingers on their wrist, thumb on their palm side for control.
The figure-four lock should be at your own wrist, not theirs — this gives you maximum leverage.
Keep their elbow bent throughout — a straight arm can pull free from the Kimura.
The finish is a rotation: bring their elbow toward your belly button while turning your shoulders away from them.
nextStep: After the Kimura system, learn the armbar system and baratoplata to chain with the Kimura.
fixItFast: Arm keeps straightening? Pull their elbow toward you to re-bend it.
Can't finish? Rotate your shoulders more — the finish is shoulder rotation, not arm pull.
They defend by grabbing their belt? Switch to the armbar or omoplata.
